teenKit.tldr: We used to think human history moved in a straight line from superstition to secular logic, but global data shows religion isn't fading at all. Instead, it's rapidly mutating, growing, and adapting to modern life.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding why belief systems endure helps us decode how humans form tribes, find meaning, and coordinate societies without falling for outdated myths about human progress.
keyTakeaways: The linear secularization theory assumes that as society gets smarter and more scientific, religion naturally dies out, but cross-national datasets prove this narrative is completely false.
Human brains are wired through evolutionary psychology to look for patterns, existential coordination, and moral frameworks that raw logic alone rarely satisfies.
Religion globally is not turning into a museum artifact; it is exploding, morphing, and outgrowing secularism on a massive scale.

vocab.meaning: The old academic assumption that modernization and science will automatically cause religion to fade away.
The way shared beliefs and rituals help large groups of people trust each other and agree on right versus wrong.
The built-in mental traits and survival mechanisms our brains developed over thousands of years of human history.
A major trend happening right in front of experts that they completely miss because of their own biases.
